column1: # questions.tsv — the ONE question schema for the single-node profile.
#   D6. Data, not code, and read by TWO commands so a new dependency is a new
#   ROW rather than a new prompt in one place and a new check in another:
#     ./setup.sh configure   ASKS every row whose `when` holds
#     ./setup.sh check       VALIDATES them (answers section): a required key
#                            left blank is a USERACTION naming it, a set key
#                            failing its validator is a FAIL with the reason
#   Rows are in ASK ORDER. Groups are asked in the order they first appear;
#   COLUMNS, tab-separated, `-` where a field is empty:
#     key        the .env key. It must also have a line in .env.example
#     group      identity | features | network | mirrors | llm | paths | advanced
#     prompt     plain English, ONE sentence, saying what the seam MEANS and,
#                for a mirror, the SHAPE expected (host prefix vs full URL)
#     default    the value a blank answer takes. `@state` is the one dynamic
#     required   y = setup cannot run without it. NO row is required today
#                (v2.45.1): every question has a working default or a
#                documented blank meaning, and the upstream LLM keys are an
#                OPTIONAL shortcut past the llm phase's LiteLLM-UI pause — the
#                UI is the primary way the catalog gets filled in, the same
#                methodology the k3s profile uses. The column stays because
#                `configure` and `check` both read it, and the next genuinely
#                unanswerable dependency is a `y` here rather than new code
#     validator  a v_* function in questions-lib.sh, or `-` for none. It prints
#                ONE line of reason on failure and is never allowed to write
#                against the answers so far. NOT bash — see q_when_holds
#     secret     y = read with no echo, and the diff prints `(secret, not printed)`
#   Blank is a VALID answer for a non-required key: a blank mirror means the
#   public source, which is the whole point of the fan-out.

column3: prompt
What should the agents call you? Leave it blank and the cockpit asks on first run
Install n8n? It is needed only by an n8n-backed integration, which today means Gmail (1 = yes, 0 = no)
Install the browser-rendering crawl service? Its image is built locally and is large (Chromium); plain HTTP fetch still works without it (1/0)
Install the agent sandbox? On this profile its backend is rootless podman, which is weaker isolation than the k3s profile's gVisor (1/0)
Install the bundled speech engine behind cc-tts/cc-stt? 0 means you point both aliases at engines of your own instead (1/0)

EWS endpoint of an on-premises Microsoft Exchange mailbox, as a full URL like https://mail.corp.example/ews/exchange.asmx — setting it (with the username and password below) routes mail and calendar to Exchange instead of the n8n Gmail façade; blank = no Exchange
The Exchange login for NTLM, as DOMAIN\\user or a UPN like user@corp.example; blank = no Exchange
Its password, never printed and never logged; blank = no Exchange
The mailbox's primary SMTP address — needed only when the username above is DOMAIN\\user rather than a UPN; blank = use the username
Is no public package index reachable at all? 1 makes the app phase install from requirements.lock instead of resolving (1/0)
Mandatory egress proxy for host-side downloads, as a full URL like http://proxy.corp.example:8080 — blank if there is none, and credentials belong in ~/.netrc

Path to a PEM bundle this install trusts INSTEAD of the system trust store, so it must contain EVERY CA the install will meet — your corporate root, plus the public roots when any mirror below is left blank (Linux: cat corporate.pem /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt > bundle.pem); blank if the public CAs are enough
Turn TLS verification OFF everywhere this install reaches? Prefer the CA above; every command then prints one WARN naming what it covers (1/0)
Mirror HOST for docker.io images — a host or host:port with no scheme and no path, like registry.corp.example; blank = docker.io
Mirror HOST for ghcr.io images (LiteLLM, the speech engine) — a host, no scheme; blank = ghcr.io
Mirror HOST for mcr.microsoft.com (the crawler's Playwright base) — a host, no scheme; blank = mcr.microsoft.com
PyPI simple-index URL for the venv and the image builds — a full URL like https://mirror.corp.example/pypi/simple; blank = pypi.org
Where uv downloads a CPython 3.12 when this host has none — a full URL, and file:// works; blank = the public python-build-standalone mirror
npm registry URL for the cockpit build — a full URL like https://mirror.corp.example/npm/; blank = registry.npmjs.org
Debian archive URL for the two image builds that apt-get — a full URL like https://mirror.corp.example/debian; blank = deb.debian.org
Debian SECURITY archive URL, a separate path on every mirror — a full URL like https://mirror.corp.example/debian-security; blank = build without the security suite
Hugging Face mirror URL for the speech engine's model snapshots — a full URL; blank = huggingface.co, and pre-placed snapshots need neither

OPTIONAL shortcut: the OpenAI-compatible /v1 base URL THIS HOST can reach, which lets setup register the aliases itself and lets check prove the LLM before anything is deployed — blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it
Its API key, never printed and never logged — use none if the server ignores keys; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it

The UPSTREAM model id for chat, meaning what the server itself calls the model rather than the alias — this is the one alias the agents address; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it

The upstream model id for knowledge-graph extraction, which must accept json_schema output — typically the same model as chat; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it

The upstream EMBEDDING model id — its dimension is measured rather than declared, and is effectively permanent once the graph index exists; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it

The upstream model id for the graph reranker, which graphiti_core addresses by that literal alias name — any chat model serves; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it

The upstream model id for text-to-speech — with the BUNDLED engine leave this blank: the llm phase registers cc-tts against it from CC_SPEECH_TTS_MODEL, and this key is only for a TTS server of your own; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it

The upstream model id for speech-to-text — with the BUNDLED engine leave this blank: the llm phase registers cc-stt against it from CC_SPEECH_STT_MODEL, and this key is only for a Whisper server of your own; blank = enter the provider in the LiteLLM UI when the llm phase pauses for it
Where this install keeps its logs, diagnostics, manifests and pid files — outside the checkout, so git status stays clean
Loopback port for the API (uvicorn)
Loopback port for the cockpit server (the Node process boot starts)
Loopback port for the spine's Postgres
Loopback port for the LiteLLM proxy and its UI
Loopback port for LiteLLM's own Postgres
Loopback port for Graphiti's MCP endpoint
Loopback port for Neo4j's bolt protocol
Loopback port for Neo4j's HTTP browser
Loopback port for n8n, used only with the n8n profile on
Loopback port for the crawl service
